title: Insight 1: Nov 8 ride had intense power spikes
description: Your Nov 8 ride hit a 10‑second max of 579 W and a max HR of 186 bpm, but the average HR of 152 bpm stayed nicely in Z2. Those short bursts are fun, just keep them brief so they don’t turn an easy day into a hard one.

title: Insight 2: Nov 12 long ride carried solid climbing
description: The 50 km ride on Nov 12 packed 506 m of elevation (≈10 m/km) over 2 hours — a good rolling challenge for Kolhapur. Your normalized power of 184 W (86 % FTP) shows you handled the hills efficiently without overdoing it.

title: Insight 3: Three rides in five days (Nov 12‑18) raise density flag
description: You rode on Nov 12, 14, and 18 with only one rest day between each. Combined with the very poor sleep on Nov 15 (3 h 12 m), this cluster could delay recovery. Consider inserting an extra easy day or a full rest day after such blocks.

title: Insight 4: Cycling VO₂max climbed from 49 to 51 in three weeks
description: Garmin shows your cycling VO₂max rising steadily: 49.0 on Nov 5 → 51.0 on Nov 18. That’s a clear sign your aerobic engine is responding well to the consistent riding — keep the momentum with mostly easy volume.

title: Insight 5: HR and power zones may need realignment
description: Your HR zones are based on LTHR 175 bpm, while power zones use an estimated FTP of 213 W (from 95 % of your 224 W 20‑min effort). The old Garmin FTP of 271 W is stale. A short ramp test or 20‑min effort would sync both zone systems and make training targets more accurate.

title: Insight 6: Weekly intensity balance looks nicely polarized
description: Across the last seven rides, average HRs mostly sat in Z1‑Z2 (104‑152 bpm) with only brief excursions higher. That roughly matches an 80/20 easy/hard split — great for joyful, sustainable improvement. Just watch that the ‘hard’ 20 % stays purposeful, not accidental.

title: Insight 7: Nov 15 sleep crash (3 h 12 m) dragged readiness down
description: Readiness dropped to 65 after that night, and HRV fell to 62 ms. The following day you still rode 51 km on Nov 14, but the short ride on Nov 19 (12 km, avg HR 104) suggests your body asked for a break. Prioritize 7+ hours sleep before harder days.

title: Insight 8: Your 10‑second sprint power touched 579 W (Nov 8)
description: That’s a strong maximal burst for a casual rider — about 2.7 × your estimated FTP. If you enjoy the occasional town‑sign sprint, keep it playful; no structured sprint sessions needed unless you want to sharpen that top end.

title: Insight 9: Add one weekly VO₂max interval to boost the 51 further
description: Try a simple session: warm up 15 min, then 4‑5 × 3 min at 110‑115 % FTP (≈235‑245 W) with 3 min easy spin recovery, cool down 10 min. Do this once a week on a fresh day — it’s the most time‑efficient way to nudge VO₂max higher.

title: Insight 10: Schedule an FTP check to update your 213 W estimate
description: Your current FTP comes from 95 % of a 20‑min effort (224 W on Nov 12), not a dedicated test. A 20‑min all‑out or a ramp test every 6‑8 weeks will keep zones honest and let you track true progress. Pick a low‑stress weekend and treat it like a fun challenge.
